Detailed method

One seeded sourdough loaf. Currently 500 g flour, 80% hydration, 22% starter, 2.2% salt, and 0% yeast. That is 400 g water, 110 g starter, 11 g salt, 1021 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 82% effective hydration. Currently 1 loaf of 1021 g. Soak the seeds in part of that water before the mix. The seeds are extra and are not in the gram total. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Seeds Soak 80 g of seeds, 16% of the flour, in 80 g of the 400 g dough water for at least 30 minutes. Use the soaked seeds and all of that water in the mix. The seeds are extra and are not in the gram total.
  2. Starter Use 110 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total.
  3. Mix Stir 500 g flour, the rest of the 400 g water, the soaked seeds, the 110 g starter and 11 g salt until no dry flour remains. At 80% the dough is sticky. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  4. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for about 3 to 4 hours. Give it three folds in the first 90 minutes. It is ready when it has grown by about half.
  5. Shape Tighten the 1021 g into one oval. This batch is 1 loaf. Set it seam-side up in a floured basket. The default 1021 g uses a round lidded pot about 24 cm across. If you change the amount, use a pot sized to fit, or split the dough. A few extra seeds on the outside are not in the gram total.
  6. Proof Cover it for 45 to 70 minutes, until it looks puffy. With 22% starter, bake it if the top starts to sink.
  7. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with a lidded pot. Score once down the length. Bake 20 minutes covered, then 18 to 24 minutes uncovered, until the crust is deep brown. Cool on a rack for at least 1 hour.
